transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi, doctor. Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been taking on a lot lately. Maybe too much. I keep starting these plans and projects—work initiatives, certification schedules, upgrading things at home, reaching out to old contacts—and at first it feels productive, you know? Like I’m being proactive.

But then it kind of… keeps going past what’s reasonable, and I don’t always notice until my wife or my director tells me I need to slow down or stop. I don’t mean to be difficult. I just have a hard time putting the brakes on once I get going.
When you’re in the middle of these projects and feeling really productive, do you find that you need less sleep than usual—like you can get by on just a few hours a night without feeling tired?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but there have been stretches where I’ll sleep maybe three hours and then wake up really sharp, like at 3 or 4 in the morning. And instead of feeling wiped out, it feels almost like I’ve been given extra time to get things done.

I know that probably doesn’t sound ideal, but in the moment it feels productive, not like I’m tired or dragging.
Have there been times when you felt unusually upbeat, energized, or even irritable — not just productive, but maybe a bit 'wired' or on edge, like you couldn't sit still or slow down your thoughts?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I usually tell myself I’m just motivated, but there are weeks where I feel kind of… electric, like I can handle anything and I don’t want to stop.

And then, honestly, if something small gets in the way—like a delay at work, or my wife asking me to slow down or explain what I’m doing—I can get sharper than I mean to. It feels in the moment like people are trying to hold me back on purpose, even though I know that probably isn’t fair.
Have there been times when you felt you needed even less sleep than usual—so little that others might have expected you to be exhausted, but you weren’t?

Yeah… there have been times like that. I don’t want to overstate it, but I’ll get maybe three hours of sleep, wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning feeling really sharp, and it’s not like I’m dragging the next day.

At the time it almost feels like… bonus time, I guess. Like I’ve been handed a few extra hours to get things done. I know that probably sounds a little concerning, but in the moment I don’t feel exhausted.

Have there been periods when you’ve taken on more projects or been more involved in activities than usual—like starting new work initiatives, diving into personal projects, or even being more socially active—more than you typically would be?

Yeah… yes, I have. I try to frame it as being organized or ambitious, because some of it is genuinely useful, but it can get away from me.

I’ll suddenly have a whole work plan mapped out, then a certification schedule, then I’m upgrading things at home like the network setup, and then I’m messaging old contacts about ideas or opportunities. It feels productive at first, like I’m finally getting everything moving.

But then it becomes… a lot. I’ll keep adding pieces and pushing past what’s reasonable until my wife tells me I need to stop, or at work my director has to kind of step in and narrow me back down. I guess that’s part of why I came in, because I don’t seem to have a great off switch when it starts.

Have there been distinct periods of time—days or even weeks—where your mood was noticeably different from your usual self, where you felt unusually high, elated, or even extremely irritable, along with this increased drive to get things done?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t know if I’d call it “high” exactly, but there are definitely some weeks where I feel almost electric, like I’m unstoppable and I can push through anything.

And I know this doesn’t sound great, but during those times even a small delay or my wife just asking me a question can make me snap. In my head it feels like everyone’s trying to slow me down on purpose, even if part of me knows that’s probably not true.

Have there been times when this feeling of being 'electric' or unstoppable lasted for several days in a row—like four days or more—where it wasn’t just a momentary mood but something that stayed with you most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… I think it has lasted several days, not just an hour or two. I’m a little hesitant to say it that strongly, because I don’t want to make it sound like I’m totally out of control, but there are stretches where for most of the day I feel kind of… wired, or electric, like I can handle anything.

And then, during those same stretches, I can get really irritated over things that probably aren’t a big deal. Like if there’s a small delay, or my wife asks me something when I’m focused, I can snap because it feels like people are slowing me down on purpose. I know that may not be fair, but in the moment it feels very real.

Have there been times when this wired or electric feeling, along with the increased energy and irritability, lasted for a full week or more — like seven days straight where you felt this way most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but there have been some weeks where it’s not just a day or two. It’s like most of the week I feel really charged up, almost electric, like I can just keep pushing and get everything done.

And then I’m more on edge too. A small delay, or my wife asking me something when I’m focused, can make me snap more than I should. In the moment it feels like people are slowing me down on purpose, even though I know that probably sounds… not totally fair.
Have there been times when you felt this way — really charged up, almost electric, and more irritable — every day for a whole week or longer, not just for a day or two?

Yeah… yes, I think there have been times like that for a whole week or longer. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but some weeks I really do feel almost electric, like I’m unstoppable and I can just push through everything.

And I get more irritable than I’d like to admit. Even a tiny delay, or my wife asking me a simple question, can make me snap because it feels like everyone’s trying to slow me down on purpose. I know that probably sounds harsh, but that’s what it feels like in the moment.

Have there been times when this increased energy and irritability affected your ability to function normally—like at work, at home, or in relationships—because you were so focused on these projects or feeling so 'wired' all the time?

Yeah… I mean, I’d like to say I was still managing it, because I really was trying to keep everything together. But yes, it has affected things.

At work, I got so locked in on a migration project and pushing it forward that when it didn’t go right… I was put on leave after it failed. That’s hard to say, because I don’t want it to sound like I’m careless or something. I was trying to fix everything, but I think being that wired didn’t help.

And at home, my wife has had to step in more than she should—around spending, me working late at night, and conversations that start normal but turn into arguments. I don’t like putting that on her.

I’ve also kind of pulled back from things I used to be more consistent with, like church music, climbing, and mentoring. Not because I don’t care, but because I can’t always reliably show up or follow through when I’m like that.

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but there are stretches like that.

I’ll wake up and just feel… heavy, I guess. Like this failed version of myself, if that makes sense. Not necessarily dramatic every second, but flat and hopeless for a lot of the day.

And things I normally can handle feel like too much. Even my wife asking me normal questions can feel overwhelming, and then I feel bad because she’s not doing anything wrong. I don’t know if that answers it the right way, but… yeah, it can last for a while.
